title: John's Smoked Ribs

items: 2 racks pork baby back ribs (about 5 to 6 lb total)
¾ to 1 cup packed brown sugar
¼ tsp cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps: Set the ribs bone side up on a rimmed baking sheet. Slide a butter knife under the thin membrane on the back of each rack, grab it with a paper towel, and peel it off in one piece.
In a medium bowl, mix the ¾ to 1 cup brown sugar, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, oregano, dry mustard, cumin, cayenne and árbol chile until no clumps of sugar remain.
Rub the olive oil all over both racks. Press the rub generously onto every side of the ribs. Wrap each rack tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hr and up to 24 hr.
Start the smoker and bring it to 225°F, keeping it between 200°F and 250°F the whole cook. Unwrap the ribs and discard the plastic.
Place the ribs bone side down on the smoker grate. Smoke uncovered for 3 hr, until the surface is deep reddish brown and the rub has set into a dry crust.

Move the ribs to the baking sheet. Drizzle the honey over the meaty side and spread it evenly, then pat the ½ cup brown sugar over the honey. Wrap each rack tightly in a double layer of heavy-duty foil.

Return the wrapped ribs to the smoker and cook for at least 3 hr more, until an instant-read thermometer between the bones reads 195°F to 203°F and the probe slides in with almost no resistance. Pork is safe at 145°F, but ribs need the higher temperature to turn tender. Cook longer if you want them even softer.
Remove the ribs, rest them in the foil for 10 min, then unwrap carefully, watching for steam, and slice between the bones.
tips: Use spare ribs instead of baby backs if you like; add about 1 hr to the wrapped stage.
Mix the rub up to 1 month ahead and store it airtight at room temperature.
Check the smoker temperature every hour, since letting it climb past 250°F can burn the sugar in the rub.
storage: Refrigerate wrapped in foil up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat in foil in a 300°F oven for 20 to 30 min, until hot through.
